text:
Alex M.: Hey support — we're seeing a bunch of 429s during short spikes even though monthly quota looks fine. Happened around 10:10am PDT. Example response headers attached below.
Priya S.: Thanks Alex — can you paste the raw response headers and a short repro? Also do you have the x-redwood-burst-credits header?
Alex M.: Sure — curl output:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 120/min
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 37
x-redwood-burst-credits: 0
retry-after: 30
content-type: application/json
```
This was from a 30s spike where we sent ~150 requests in 10s. We expected burst credits to absorb that.
Jamal O.: quick primer: our infra uses a token-bucket with per-account refill (baseline) and a credit bank for short bursts. Bank max is 120 credits, refills at baseline rate. If bank is 0 you see 429s during spikes. Smoothing policy also does cluster-level smoothing to prevent noisy neighbors.
Priya S.: Helpful. Alex — can you run this repro script? It uses 200 concurrent reqs in 10s which should trigger the behaviour:
```
# bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$API_URL/generate" &
done
wait
```
Also check if you're using multiple API keys from same account; bursts are per-customer not per-key.
Alex M.: Running now. Also noticed long tails on latency when traffic hits the limit.
Carlos Ops: @Priya S. FYI we can temporarily bump account burst_credits to 2x for 1h from the console while we investigate. That usually prevents immediate 429s. Long term we should either move them to Dedicated or tune autoscale and smoothing.
Priya S.: Steps for support resolution:
1) Ask customer to add exponential backoff with jitter; typical: initial 200-500ms, doubling, plus jitter.
2) Use connection pooling/keep-alive; avoid spawning new TCP per request.
3) If traffic is truly spiky, request temporary burst increase (we'll do now) or suggest Dedicated.
4) We'll collect metrics: burst_credit_balance, x-rate-limit-remaining, and request ids.
Alex M.: Back with logs — reproduced. x-redwood-burst-credits went to 0 then 429s. Script included details and request-ids. Thanks for the temp bump — no more 429s.
Jamal O.: We'll open a follow-up ticket for infra: investigate whether refill rate or bank cap needs adjusting for this customer’s profile. Also log shows their pattern is many short spikes; propose smoothing window change from 60s to 30s on the bank to allow faster refill for short bursts (but this can raise noise for other tenants).
Priya S.: Closing loop with customer: we'll keep monitoring for 24h, advise about smoothing changes only if needed. Alex — can you confirm if traffic originates from a single host or multiple regions? That affects per-conn keep-alive behavior.
Alex M.: Single region. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Support Bot: Ticket #4321 created and assigned to eng-infra. ETA 48h for triage. :sparkles:
